title: Load more list with optional infinite scroll
when: The user wants a list that shows a first batch and loads more items on a button press or near the end of the scroll.
inputs: the items or a local JSON file
prompt:
Goal: A list that appends batches through one function, keeps keyboard focus sensible and always leaves the footer reachable.
Steps:
1. Render the first batch of N items in a <ul>, then <button type="button">Load more</button> below it.
2. loadMore() takes the next N items from the array, or from fetch of a relative JSON file with JSON.parse errors caught, and builds each li with createElement.
3. While loading set aria-busy="true" on the list and disable the button; afterwards move focus to the first new item (tabindex="-1").
4. Announce Showing 20 of 48 in a role="status" region; at the end hide the button and say All 48 shown.
5. Infinite scroll: an IntersectionObserver on a sentinel calls the same loadMore(), stops after 3 automatic loads and leaves the button.
Quality bar:
- The count of shown and total is always visible.
- Failures show a Retry button, not a silent stop.
- Scroll position does not jump on append.
Pitfalls:
- Endless loading that makes the footer unreachable.
- Items built with innerHTML from data.
- Several loads firing at once.
Verify:
- [ ] The button has a type and a clear label.
- [ ] The status region updates after each batch.
- [ ] Focus moves to the new items.
- [ ] Loading stops at the end.
Output: List markup, list.css and load-more.js, plus items.json when the data is separate.

examples.input: lista de posts com botao carregar mais
examples.output: ul with 10 posts, Load more adds 10 from posts.json, status Showing 20 of 46, focus on the first new post
